title: Tony Parenti at Jimmy Ryan's and being let go
summary: Parenti's band with Max Kaminsky and Bobby Pratt was dismissed at Ryan's around 1968-70.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, what about during the time of the 1960's. Of course, socially there's a lot of upheaval and so forth, and new musical styles had come on the scene. Before you
Moore (III) - 83
started working with Tony Parenti, who did you work with?
Tony Parenti...
Yeah, you worked with Tony Parenti in '68...
Yeah, down at Jimmy Ryan's.
From 1968 to 1970.

I did some things after Jimmy Ryan's that were freelancing. I did a lot of different things over in Jersey, New Jersey. A place called Ramson(?) or something like that... All them different places over there, freelancing, you know...
Rahway? I'm trying to think of...
Ramsville, a place called Ramsville(?) there or something?
I'll have to look that one up. I'm not sure about that. But anyway, you did some freelancing.
Freelancing and... Well, after we left Jimmy Ryan's, after... Something happened in Jimmy Ryan's. They let Tony Parenti out.
Yeah? Out of Jimmy Ryan's?

They let him out and they let me out at the same time, and they took another band. That's when they brought Zutty Singleton in there. Yeah, it was Zutty... And they put Max Kaminsky in charge of the band.
Max was in the band with Tony.
Moore (III) - 84
Yeah, he was in the band with Tony. So Tony... Max always wanted to be the leader of that band. But I don't know what happened...
I see.
Of course, Tony was hitting the jug kinda hard, you know. But he wouldn't have hit it that hard, though, if he had a good band there. He could play, too.
Who else was in that band besides you, Max and Tony?
A trombone player who played piano in the band.
Bobby Pratt?
Bobby Pratt was playing piano.
Who was playing bass?
I don't remember who was playing bass. Was it Pops Foster...? No.
I think Pops died in '69. I don't think he was...

Well, they had some bass players there. I think they had two or three bass players there. Right now I don't think it's the same one... I think they're still down there. I can't think of the name of the bass player.
All right, then...
After Jimmy Ryan's, three weeks later, we was doing some things over in Jersey, then he come back and he
Moore (III) - 85
had a chance to go in the next block, 52nd Street... No, not the next block. Well, 52nd Street, right by the union, where our 802 Union used to be. It ain't there no more.
It's in the same building as the Roseland.
Yeah, same building.
Then it's 53rd Street.
52nd Street.
Is that 52nd Street?
Yes.
Okay.
[END OF TAPE 5, SIDE A]
